input.prompt:
A candid, ordinary city photograph at dusk under low cloud, the kind a street photographer takes in passing: A billboard stands beside a concrete motorway overpass at dusk in thick fog.

The output is one single photograph, landscape 16:9.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera from the road below at billboard height, 70mm lens, f/2.8, square to it. The billboard fills about 50 percent of the frame width, sharp; the dark concrete underside of the overpass crosses the top of the frame; car headlights blur into soft streaks on the wet road below; the fog closes in behind it. It is an ordinary, everyday billboard of standard proportions, about three times as wide as it is tall, nothing special about its structure. The mist and cloud stay far behind the design surface: it is crisp and clear, with nothing soft, hazy or glowing over its face or edges. Nobody is in frame.

Place: A real city at late dusk in thick low fog: the fog sits low and heavy, swallowing the upper floors and everything a block behind the billboard or screen into soft grey; wet stone and asphalt; small warm lights blur into halos in the fog. The fog is one even, dense layer, never swirling banks, and never in front of the design surface.

Light: Late blue-grey dusk under thick fog, darker than before; the billboard or screen is the brightest thing in the frame and makes a soft glow in the fog around it; street lights are soft halos.

Palette and grade: The same grade on every image: muted desaturated greys and charcoal, a slight cool tint in the cloud, small warm sodium lights, deep but not crushed shadows; the design surface pure neutral white. Like an overcast civic square at dusk on a smoggy day: flat grey-brown sky, muted stone, silhouetted people, the screen glowing clean.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph in a real city, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, never a tiny screen in a wide view. It is an unstaged photograph of a real place on a real day, with small honest signs of weather and age on the place only; the design surface itself is new and clean. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. Exposure is honest, but the design surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation or bloom around lights.

Design surface: THE BILLBOARD FACE IS PLAIN PAPER-WHITE, evenly lit by its lamps edge to edge, flat and taut with crisp corners inside its thin dark frame, nothing printed on it and nothing crossing it.

Finish: Shot on 35mm Kodak Portra 800 pushed one stop in low light: visible natural grain, muted soft film colour, slight lens falloff, honest underexposed dusk. Moody but believable, like a real photograph from a real evening; never a render, never cinematic teal and orange.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, mist, haze or glow over or around the design surface, any object not named in the shot, layered or swirling fog banks, a clean smooth digital look.
